purpose: Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like a runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It can help with both seasonal allergies (like hay fever) and year-round allergies caused by things like dust mites or pet dander. It is also used to treat a skin condition called chronic hives (urticaria).
how_it_works: When your body encounters something you are allergic to, it releases a chemical called histamine, which causes those annoying allergy symptoms. Levocetirizine blocks the receptors in your body that histamine attaches to, so it cannot trigger those symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock cover over a keyhole so the key (histamine) cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, so be careful when driving or using machinery. You might also experience dry mouth, tiredness, headache, or a sore throat. Some people feel a bit dizzy or have a stuffy nose.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can make drowsiness much worse. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or advise against using it. It is generally not recommended for children under 6 months old. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills or anxiety medications. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
typical_dosing: For most adults and children 12 years and older, the usual dose is 5 mg (one tablet) taken once a day in the evening. For younger children (6 months to 11 years), the dose is lower and depends on the child's age and weight, so always follow your doctor's instructions. It can be taken with or without food, and it is best taken at the same time each day.
